# Northgate Clinic account profile (Jan–Jun 2026)

**Short version:** Northgate Clinic appears as two account IDs, and the data has gaps that limit what you can say about it. The log is at `work/exploration-log.md`.

## Who the account is
- **ACC-1042, Northgate Clinic.** `accounts.csv` shows it valid 2025-01-01 to 2026-03-31.
- **ACC-1077, Northgate Health Partners (formerly Northgate Clinic).** Valid from 2026-04-01.
- **The link between the two is inferred.** It rests on the "formerly" in the name. No table maps one ID to the other, so I treated both as one entity.

## What the records show

| Month | Account | Plan | Billed volume | Amount | Contract status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Jan | 1042 | standard | 1,840 | $772.80 | active |
| Feb | 1042 | no billing row | no billing row | no billing row | paused |
| Mar | 1042 | enterprise-annual | 1,910 | $592.10 | active |
| Apr | 1077 | enterprise-annual | 1,120 | $347.20 | active |
| May | 1077 | enterprise-annual | 1,085 | $336.35 | active |
| Jun | 1077 | no billing row | no billing row | no billing row | no status row |

Volume is billed volume. The per-unit price is about $0.42 on the standard plan in January and $0.31 on enterprise-annual from March through May.

**Tickets (6 in total):**
- ACC-1042: a feature request on 01-08, a feature request on 03-11, and an integration ticket on 03-26.
- ACC-1077: billing questions on 04-01 and 04-04, and an outage report on 05-25.

## Changes over time
These are dated changes. The records don't say whether any of them caused another.
- **February:** the contract status was paused, and there is no billing row for the month.
- **2026-03-01:** the plan changed from standard to enterprise-annual (`plan_changes.csv`). The per-unit price was lower in March than in January.
- **2026-04-01:** the account ID and name changed. Billed volume went from 1,910 in March to 1,120 in April, down about 41%. Two billing-question tickets were opened on 04-01 and 04-04.
- **Attribution is unresolved.** If you want any of these explained, such as the volume drop or the billing tickets, that is a separate investigation.

## Data-quality issues
- **Missing months:**
  - There is no February billing row for 1042.
  - There is no June billing row for 1077.
  - **February (1042):** the status is "paused", which fits with no billing. Nothing outside the billing data confirms it.
  - **June (1077):** I can't tell whether June was no activity, an unrecorded bill, or an incomplete export. Other accounts do have June billing rows, so the billing export doesn't look truncated overall.
- **Contract status stops at May for every account.** That export looks truncated, so Northgate's June status is unknown.
- **Nothing after March for 1042.** That matches the `valid_to` date in `accounts.csv`, but that is the same table making the claim, so it isn't independent evidence.
- **No plan-change record for ACC-1077.** It shows up on enterprise-annual from its first row, which fits it being a successor account. The data doesn't say.

## Not checked
- Whether the drop from 1,910 to 1,120 units is real or reflects only part of the volume moving to the new account.
- Whether the new account's volume is the same business as the old one. I only have the name link.
- Anything about June.

The most useful follow-ups are to ask the contracts and billing owners for June and for the February rows, and to confirm the 1042→1077 mapping.
